normalized_issues.title: Session lock after DHF append failure — operational risk of permanent availability failure requiring manual SQL intervention

merged_from.title: Persistent DHF session lock creates permanent availability failure requiring manual SQL intervention

normalized_issues.core_problem: R1 fixed the durability gap (lock now persists via locked_at/lock_reason columns). The remaining concern is that any transient DB outage or retry exhaustion permanently locks the session with no automated unlock path, no operator dashboard, and no circuit-breaker. For a medtech production target this is a significant operational risk, though for hackathon scope it is acceptable as documented. The 'never descopable' gate is appropriate for correctness; the missing piece is an unlock/recovery operator API.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: 'Reopening requires manual intervention (operator closes the session via SQL, reconciles the model state, and starts a new session).' — SPEC-00 Seam C
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a documented operator unlock API (even a CLI command or SQL procedure) with audit trail. Clarify that the 'never descopable' gate applies to the lock behavior, not to the absence of an unlock path. For v1/hackathon, document the SQL unlock procedure explicitly.

normalized_issues.title: Recovery screenshot PNG bytes defined in RecoveryEventContext but never written to dhf.entries BYTEA columns

merged_from.title: Recovery-event append path drops PNG bytes added to the new DHF schema
Recovery screenshot bytes are defined but never written

normalized_issues.core_problem: Migration 008 adds screenshot_before_png/screenshot_after_png BYTEA columns. RecoveryEventContext carries byte[]? ScreenshotBeforePng/ScreenshotAfterPng. However, AppendRecoveryEventAsync (§7.2) builds a DhfTurnContext with ScreenshotBeforePath = null and ScreenshotAfterPath = null and never passes the PNG byte arrays through to persistence. The R1 fix is incomplete: deep validation and viewer rendering for recovery events still cannot rely on screenshot bytes being present.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-04 §7.2: 'ScreenshotBeforePath = null, ScreenshotAfterPath = null' — PNG byte arrays from RecoveryEventContext are silently dropped.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Extend DhfTurnContext to carry optional PNG byte payloads (or add a dedicated recovery insert path), and ensure AppendRecoveryEventAsync writes ScreenshotBeforePng/ScreenshotAfterPng into dhf.entries. Add a test asserting the BYTEA columns are populated for recovery events.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer UUID-as-capability access control: knowing one session UUID reveals all tenant sessions via sidebar

merged_from.title: Viewer UUID capability as sole access control is brittle against leakage or sharing in adversarial sharing scenarios
Viewer capability-based session listing has no matching read-only repository API

normalized_issues.core_problem: Two distinct sub-problems: (1) SDR-TL-012 explicitly acknowledges that knowing one session UUID reveals all sessions for that tenant via the sidebar — this is a security exposure for CAD design data. (2) IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ListSessionsAsync takes tenantId, not a sessionId capability, so the viewer cannot implement the capability-based access model without undocumented tenant-resolution logic. The R1 fix (neutral landing page, removed ?tenant= override) addressed the anonymous enumeration path but not the sidebar exposure or the repository API gap.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-TL-012: 'knowing one session UUID for a tenant reveals all sessions for that tenant via the sidebar (acceptable for hackathon; v1.5 Clerk resolves this).' SPEC-04 §9.2: ListSessionsAsync(string tenantId, ...) — no sessionId-capability overload.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ListSessionsForCapabilityAsync(Guid sessionId) that resolves tenant from the session and returns authorized sessions. For the security exposure, either implement Clerk now (documented as 15-30 min) or explicitly scope the sidebar to show only the single accessed session in v1.

normalized_issues.title: RecoveryEventContext structured fields collapsed to free-text RawTranscript — structured recovery data is unqueryable

merged_from.title: RecoveryEventContext is not persisted as structured recovery data

normalized_issues.core_problem: RecoveryEventContext defines structured fields (Trigger, Strategy, Success, FailureReason, ModelStateDivergenceDescription) but AppendRecoveryEventAsync collapses them into a free-text description string written to RawTranscript. Viewer logic, validation, reporting, and audit queries cannot reliably filter or consume recovery outcomes from an ad-hoc string. This is a new issue distinct from R1-ISSUE-004 (which was about the absence of any recovery storage — now resolved). The current gap is that storage exists but is unstructured.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-04 §7.2: 'var description = $"Recovery event: trigger={context.Trigger}, strategy={context.Strategy}, success={context.Success}"' written to RawTranscript.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a recovery_context JSONB column to dhf.entries (or a separate dhf.recovery_events table), include it in hash coverage, and expose it in EntryDetail read DTO. AppendRecoveryEventAsync should write structured fields directly.

normalized_issues.title: Heartbeat timeout specifies illegal WebSocket close code 1006 — RFC 6455 forbids sending it in a close frame

merged_from.title: Heartbeat timeout specifies illegal WebSocket close code 1006
Heartbeat closure uses an invalid WebSocket close code

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §12.7 specifies 'Missed pong → close with 1006 ("abnormal closure") after 2 missed intervals.' RFC 6455 §7.4.1 explicitly reserves 1006 for local reporting of abnormal closure and prohibits it from being sent in a WebSocket Close frame. .NET's ClientWebSocket will throw or substitute a different code, breaking heartbeat and reconnect behavior across implementations.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §12.7: 'Missed pong → close with 1006 ("abnormal closure") after 2 missed intervals.' RFC 6455 §7.4.2: codes 1005 and 1006 MUST NOT be set as a status code in a Close control frame.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either: (a) abort the TCP connection without sending a Close frame (the standard approach for heartbeat failure, which the peer observes as 1006 locally), or (b) send a valid close code such as 1001 (Going Away) or a custom 4xxx code with documented semantics. Update tests accordingly.

normalized_issues.title: Same-epoch reconnect accepts updated capability fields that are immutable in dhf.sessions — contradiction between SPEC-01 and SPEC-04

merged_from.title: Same-epoch reconnect behavior conflicts with immutable session metadata

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §9 states that same-AddinSessionId reconnects must 'accept the updated capability fields (AddinVersion, SwVersion, SwBuild, ScreenshotRootPath).' SPEC-04 SDR-04-010 states all dhf.sessions columns except ended_at, locked_at, and lock_reason are immutable once inserted. The guard_session_update trigger will reject any UPDATE to addin_version, sw_version, etc. There is no defined mutable store for reconnect capability updates.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §9: 'accept the updated capability fields (AddinVersion, SwVersion, SwBuild, ScreenshotRootPath).' SPEC-04 SDR-04-010: 'All columns in dhf.sessions except ended_at, locked_at, and lock_reason are immutable once inserted.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one contract: either (a) reject same-epoch reconnects when capability fields differ (simplest), or (b) add a separate mutable dhf.session_reconnects table for reconnect metadata and reference it consistently in both specs.

normalized_issues.title: API secret transmitted in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header — logged by proxies, edge platforms, and APM tooling

merged_from.title: API secret is sent in the WebSocket subprotocol header

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §12.3 places the full API credential (keyId + secret) in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header. This header is commonly logged by Railway edge, reverse proxies, APM tools, and browser devtools. Suppressing the echoed response header does not prevent request-side logging. A leaked header exposes a long-lived tenant credential.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Move the credential to an Authorization header on the HTTP upgrade request (standard practice), or issue a short-lived one-time token over HTTPS and use that in the upgrade. Define mandatory request-header redaction rules for Railway logging configuration.

normalized_issues.title: Runtime orchestrator role has DROP TRIGGER / DDL privileges — undermines DHF immutability guarantee

merged_from.title: Application role can disable the DB immutability triggers

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-04 §3.2 honestly discloses 'The orchestrator has DROP TRIGGER privilege.' This means the same runtime principal that appends DHF records can remove the trigger-based immutability protections. For a system positioned as a design audit log foundation for 21 CFR 820.30 alignment, this makes the append-only guarantee dependent on application goodwill rather than database policy.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-04 §3.2: 'The orchestrator has DROP TRIGGER privilege.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Run the orchestrator under a DML-only Postgres role (INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE on permitted columns only) with no DDL, DROP TRIGGER, or ALTER TABLE privileges. Reserve schema migrations for a separate admin role. Update the enforcement gap disclosure to reflect the corrected trust boundary.

normalized_issues.title: Unknown message type handling is contradictory: SPEC-01 requires MalformedEnvelope, SPEC-02 requires UnknownMessageType

merged_from.title: Unknown message-type handling is internally inconsistent

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §3 states an 'unrecognized' polymorphic discriminator MUST produce MalformedEnvelope. SPEC-02 §6.5 states unknown IClientMessage subtypes produce AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = UnknownMessageType). These are two different wire-level outcomes for the same condition. Interop tests and retry logic cannot be implemented deterministically.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §3: 'the polymorphic discriminator is unrecognized... the receiver MUST... Send a protocol error message with ErrorCode = MalformedEnvelope.' SPEC-02 §6.5: 'Unknown IClientMessage subtypes produce AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = UnknownMessageType).'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define one canonical mapping: malformed/unparseable envelope → MalformedEnvelope; well-formed envelope with unsupported 'type' discriminator → UnknownMessageType. Update SPEC-01 §3 and SPEC-02 §6.5 to use this split consistently, and align required tests in both specs.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer SPEC-06 declared to depend only on SPEC-04 but imports SPEC-01 types — dependency rule is contradictory

merged_from.title: Viewer dependency graph is contradictory across specs

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 §1 Module Map declares SPEC-06 depends on 'SPEC-04 (read-only)' only. SPEC-01 §18 states 'SPEC-06 imports StateSnapshot, SelectionRef, FeatureNode (for display), and nothing else.' StateSnapshot, SelectionRef, and FeatureNode are defined in SPEC-01 (BSVoiceCAD.Protocol). Architecture tests and project references cannot satisfy both statements simultaneously.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §1: 'SPEC-06 | Viewer | Depends On | SPEC-04 (read-only).' SPEC-01 §18: 'SPEC-06 imports StateSnapshot, SelectionRef, FeatureNode.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one: (a) expose viewer-needed display types entirely via SPEC-04 read model DTOs (re-projecting StateSnapshot/FeatureNode into viewer-specific records), or (b) explicitly allow SPEC-06 to depend on SPEC-01 and update the Module Map and NetArchTest rules accordingly.

normalized_issues.title: CallId format (UUIDv7) validated in SPEC-02 but never defined in SPEC-01 — wire contract gap

merged_from.title: CallId is validated as UUIDv7 without any protocol-level format definition

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §6.5 validates CallId as UUIDv7 format and SPEC-02 §10 requires CallIdFormatValidationTests. SPEC-01 §5 defines CallId only as 'Lifecycle identity (see SPEC-03)' with no format specification. Producer (orchestrator, SPEC-03) and consumer (add-in, SPEC-02) can disagree on format while both remaining spec-compliant.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §6.5: 'MessageDispatcher validates that CallId conforms to the UUIDv7 format.' SPEC-01 §5 ToolCallMessage: 'CallId: Lifecycle identity (see SPEC-03)' — no format constraint.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define the canonical CallId format (UUIDv7 string) in SPEC-01 §5 alongside MessageId. Add CallIdFormatTests to SPEC-01's required test list. Remove the format definition from SPEC-02 (it should only reference SPEC-01).

normalized_issues.title: API key lockout persistence required by v1 contract but lockout_event schema is deferred to post-hackathon

merged_from.title: API-key lockout persistence is required without any defined schema

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §12.6 specifies '10 failed attempts per hour → temporary key lockout (15 min), logged as an api_keys.lockout_event row (schema deferred to post-hackathon).' The v1 auth contract requires writing lockout events but no table or migration is defined. This cannot be implemented or migration-tested as written.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §12.6: 'logged as an api_keys.lockout_event row (schema deferred to post-hackathon).'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either define the lockout_event schema and migration now (it is a simple table), or explicitly remove the persistence requirement from v1 and implement lockout as in-memory only with a documented limitation.

normalized_issues.title: Screenshot size reduction has no defined terminal behavior after 4 iterations — oversize message has no valid wire outcome

merged_from.title: Message-size control has no defined failure path when reduction still does not fit

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §7.2 limits dimension reduction to 4 iterations and says 'Abandon after iteration 4' but does not define what message is sent. Additionally, neither spec requires checking the size of the fully serialized ToolResultMessage (screenshot + StateAfter.FeatureTree) against the 4 MiB envelope limit after reduction.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §7.2: 'Iterative halving up to 4 iterations. Abandon after iteration 4.' No defined wire outcome for the abandon case.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define the explicit terminal behavior after max reductions (e.g., return ToolError with a specific code, or send a 1x1 placeholder). Require a final full-message-size check that can trigger feature-tree truncation or a deterministic ToolError before send.

normalized_issues.title: Planned disconnect 60-second escalation timeout has no defined post-timeout action

merged_from.title: Planned disconnect leaves behavior undefined after the 60-second escalation timeout

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §9.1 states the add-in 'Waits for any currently-executing tool call to complete on the UI thread (60-second escalation timeout)' but never specifies what happens when the COM call is still running at 60 seconds. Since executing COM cannot be preempted (SPEC-00 Seam B, SPEC-02 §2.4), some implementations will hang indefinitely, others will force-close, producing divergent DHF session semantics.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §9.1: '60-second escalation timeout' with no defined post-timeout action. SPEC-02 §2.4: 'COM calls cannot be interrupted. The work runs to completion.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Specify the exact post-timeout action: e.g., log the stuck call, skip AddinTeardownMessage send (session closes via heartbeat_timeout), and force-close the WebSocket. Document the resulting DHF session closure reason.

normalized_issues.title: ACC-20 performance gate is not reproducible — no defined hardware, browser, cache state, or measurement point

merged_from.title: ACC-20 performance gate is not reproducible

normalized_issues.core_problem: ACC-20 requires 'Viewer timeline renders a 20-entry session in under 1 second on the demo laptop' but does not define the benchmark hardware profile, browser/runtime, warm vs cold cache, network conditions, or whether the 1s target is server response time, network transfer, or UI render time. CI and manual acceptance cannot produce a deterministic pass/fail.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §3: 'ACC-20 | Viewer timeline renders a 20-entry session in under 1 second on the demo laptop'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define: specific machine (GE75 or named equivalent), browser (Chrome stable), cache state (warm), measurement point (Time to Interactive from navigation start), and network (localhost or Railway prod). Add a Playwright/Lighthouse fixture to BSVoiceCAD.Tests.Integration.

normalized_issues.title: Cross-workstation conflict detection relies on client-supplied untrusted WorkstationId — ACC-19 is not reliably enforceable

merged_from.title: Cross-workstation conflict detection relies on an untrusted machine-name field

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §5 documents WorkstationId as Environment.MachineName and explicitly states 'is NOT a security trust boundary.' However, SPEC-04 SDR-04-008 and ACC-19 use WorkstationId as the basis for the hard-error cross-workstation conflict check. A spoofed or non-unique WorkstationId within a tenant can cause false positives (legitimate reconnects rejected) or false negatives (conflicts silently merged).
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §5: 'WorkstationId: Environment.MachineName... is NOT a security trust boundary.' SPEC-00 §3: 'ACC-19 | Cross-workstation AddinSessionId conflict throws CrossWorkstationSessionConflictException.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Use AddinSessionId (which incorporates MachineGuid + process ID + timestamp + nonce per SPEC-02 §8.1) as the conflict discriminator rather than WorkstationId alone. WorkstationId can remain for display/audit purposes. Update ACC-19 test definition accordingly.

dropped_findings.title: BSMS enforcement and 'no vector retrieval ever' SDR inflates complexity and creates brittle dependency
dropped_findings.reason: style_only — SDR-TL-009 is an explicit architectural decision by the document authors, not a defect. The contrarian position is noted but the SDR is locked by design and the hackathon scope explicitly carves out the exemption. No actionable defect exists in the spec as written.

dropped_findings.title: Threading and post-timeout recovery assumptions in Seam B are brittle against SolidWorks COM implementation changes
dropped_findings.reason: too_vague — The concern about SolidWorks COM nondeterminism is real but the spec already documents the Day-0 validation requirement and the SynchronizationContext probe. The 'deterministic selection rule' claim is a SPEC-03 concern not yet reviewed. Flagging as out-of-scope for SPEC-00/01/02/04 review; should be raised against SPEC-03 when reviewed.
